You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task notes

## task-1e800d92: overlap the two fields separated by a marker column

In the solved example, the input is an `H x W` grid with a single solid vertical separator/marker column. Ignore the separator; compare the equal-width fields to its left and right cell-by-cell. Produce an `H x field_width` grid: put color `2` where both corresponding cells are nonzero, otherwise `0`.

Evidence: demo had a color-4/7 left field and color-5 right field with output 2 only at positions where both sides were nonzero. Test had separator color 6, left color 4, right color 3; correct output was 2 at overlapping occupied positions and 0 elsewhere. Thus colors/patterns act as occupancy masks, and output is their intersection, not arithmetic on colors.

Additional confirmed instance (task-1e800d92): 4x9 input with solid color-9 separator at column 5 (1-indexed), splitting two 4-column fields. Correct output was 4x4: `[[0,2,0,2],[0,0,0,0],[0,2,0,0],[0,2,0,0]]`. This directly reconfirms cellwise nonzero/nonzero overlap -> 2 and all other positions -> 0; separator is removed and output width is each side's width.

### Additional confirmed instance (task-761f6fb6, 13x11)
Background was color 3 and row marks were color 6. Fill only the color-3 cells strictly between consecutive 6s in each row with color 2; preserve the marks and all cells outside each consecutive-mark span. This test had rows with alternating marks/background, including four marks (thus fill three internal gaps), as well as other rows with 2–3 marks, and two rows were unaffected because they had no marks. A 3-mark row separated by regular one-cell gaps became alternating `6,2,6,2,6`; the 4-mark row became `6,2,6,2,6,2,6`. Accepted with zero wrong attempts. Process each row independently; multiple internal gaps are all filled, but never extend past the first or last mark.

### Additional confirmed instance (task-761f6fb6, 10x13)
Background was color 6; marks were color 5. In each row, fill only the background cells strictly between consecutive color-5 marks with color 2. Leave leading/trailing background and rows without marks unchanged; preserve all mark cells. The 10x13 test had marks in rows 1, 3–7, and 9–10; row 2 and row 8 were empty. Accepted output:
`[[5,2,5,2,5,2,5,2,5,6,6,6,6],[6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6],[6,5,2,5,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6],[6,6,6,6,5,2,5,2,5,2,5,6,6],[6,6,6,6,6,6,5,2,5,2,5,6,6],[6,6,6,5,2,5,2,5,6,6,6,6,6],[6,6,6,5,2,5,6,6,6,6,6,6,6],[6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6],[6,6,6,6,6,6,6,5,2,5,2,5,6],[6,6,6,6,6,5,2,5,2,5,2,5,6]]`. Confirmed correct with zero wrong attempts, reinforcing that only internal gaps between neighboring marks are changed.

### Additional confirmed instance (task-761f6fb6, 12x10)
Background was 5 and repeated marks were 0. For each row, change only the color-5 cells strictly between consecutive color-0 marks to color 2; preserve all marks and all cells outside these internal gaps. Rows with no marks remain unchanged. In the confirmed 12x10 test, e.g. row 1 marks at columns 1, 3, 5 with gaps filled at c2 and c4; row 2 marks at c4, c6, c8 with gaps c5,c7 filled; row 7 marks at c2,c4,c6 with gaps c3,c5; row 8 marks at c2,c4,c6,c8 with gaps c3,c5,c7; row 11 marks at c3,c5,c7,c9 with gaps c4,c6,c8; row 12 marks at c2,c4,c6 with gaps c3,c5. Other internal fill locations follow the same per-row consecutive-mark rule, while leading/trailing 5s (and rows 3,10 with no marks) remain unchanged. Submission confirmed correct with zero wrong attempts. This reconfirms prior task-761f6fb6 cases across changed background/mark colors: identify the repeated mark color from the row pattern, fill only intervening background cells with 2, and never extend past the first/last mark.

### Additional confirmed instance (task-761f6fb6, 27x15)
Background color 9; marks color 8. Each row is handled independently: replace only color-9 cells strictly between consecutive color-8 marks with 2. Preserve all 8 marks and all 9 cells before the first and after the last mark; rows with no marks are unchanged. Confirmed output on a 27x15 grid with varied mark counts (including rows with 2, 3, and 4 marks) was accepted with zero wrong attempts. Useful validation: in the original rows, mark positions can be listed 1-based; fill every gap between adjacent positions only, regardless of gap length.
